target_customer: Engineering teams in AI labs, electronic design automation and GPU computing needing proofs that code is correct
problem: Formal verification used to need specialist teams and years of work. Theorem uses AI to produce proofs that can be checked in CI, so AI-written code can be trusted.
business_model: B2B software and services for automated formal verification

founders.name: Jason Gross
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on verified code that powers HTTPS connections in Chrome; VentureBeat says the work was at MIT.

founders.name: Rajashree Agrawal
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat calls her a machine learning research engineer training the verification models.

competitors.name: Harmonic
competitors.what: AI math model Aristotle that verifies output in Lean

technical_complexity.rationale: Training models to write and check formal proofs that are equivalent to reference code is research-grade. The company demoed translating 1,276 problems from Rocq to Lean.

defensibility.rationale: Rare skills in proof engineering and trained models are hard to copy quickly, but well funded rivals such as Harmonic and Axiom work on adjacent verification.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded formal verification startups grew through 2025 and 2026. A late October 2026 item says Anthropic and Theorem jointly announced bug-finding in open source, a partnership not an acquisition.

market_need_then: AI generated code was growing fast in 2025, raising demand for stronger correctness guarantees than tests. Evidence is company framing and a VentureBeat report of a bug that slipped past testing at Anthropic.

branding.domain_note: Uses theorem.dev because theorem.com and theorem.co belong to other companies per a domain article. No acquisition story found.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Minimal site with the tagline 'Verify all software.'

brand_strength.rationale: A meaningful real word that fits the product and a crisp tagline, but several other firms are called Theorem, such as TheoremOne, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Theorem raised a 6M seed led by Khosla in January 2026 about nine months after Spring 2025 YC. The founders have deep verification credentials and AI code generation made verification timely. The risks are better funded Harmonic and Axiom and the long sales cycle for formal methods.
notes: Seed confirmed by VentureBeat (27 Jan 2026) and Startupintros (29 Jan 2026). The 10,000x speedup is a company claim. Funding total beyond the seed is unknown, so coverage is partial. Prior employers for the founders were not found beyond MIT, so left empty. &Truth, Pramaana Labs and Axiom rounds are different companies.
